checks.what: Kept verdict checked on the Banu Kanz page. One correction to the reasoning: the territory list ('the countryside of Aswan to the north', 'most of the Eastern Desert between Aswan and the Red Sea') comes after the 1006 Kanz al-Dawla title, not '943' as the fixer wrote. Still, the page says that 'By the 10th century, they were running a principality that replaced that of al-Umari's', who had been pushed out of Wadi Allaqi and Aswan. It also says the allied Hadariba controlled the land between the Red Sea coast and the Nile, and that Ishaq ibn Bishr became chief 'by 943'. The Ikhshidids are not mentioned. So a local principality in the desert and around Aswan in 943-947 has support, and the size rule result can stand.

The banu-kanz 1174 and 1175 keyframes no longer draw the Sudanese Red Sea state; the Aydhab 80 km disc is kept. Checked the new banu-kanz gain and the alodia mirror loss of the Red Sea state (Sudan) in 1365, both at confidence 1. Banu Kanz page checked: the Aydhab-Suakin reach ('the region between the Red Sea ports of Aydhab and Suakin in the east') is given only for the reign of al-Ashraf Sha'ban and Yalbugha, in the account of the Mamluk expedition after Dongola fell, and 'surrendered to the Mamluk governor of Qus in December 1365'. Placing the event at 1365 as the latest year the page shows is supported. Alodia is not named on the page, so the counterpart comes from the alodia dossier's c. 950 holding, which is acceptable at confidence 1. The banu-kanz gain matches the alodia loss, so the loss is skipped and the gain takes only alodia's 605 cells. The 19 kingdom-of-kush cells in the 1365 conflict remain.

Maris (banu-kanz keyframes 1175 and 1365, ledger 1, 2, 5 and 6) is now Lower Nubia minus Aswan 50 km minus everything south of 22.9 N, 21 cells; the old spec had 177. makuria ledger 6 has the mirror loss in 1175 at confidence 1. Makuria page checked: no sentence uses 'Maris'; Turan-Shah 'conquered Qasr Ibrim in January 1173'; the Nubian army 'arrived to confront the invaders at Adindan near Faras' in 1175; Saladin's troops retreat 'out of Nubia'; in 1367 one ruler sat 'in Gebel Adda and the other ... in Qasr Ibrim'. Its 'as far south as Wadi es-Sebua' intermarriage comes after 1412/3, outside the dossier's years. So keeping the reach south of 22.9 N Makurian has support. Leftover issues (see problems): 5 of the 21 Maris cells are at 24.6-25.2 N, north of Aswan, which the old spec already had. Ledger 1, the 1174 loss to ayyubid-sultanate, now also passes 23 Aswan-governorate cells at 22.1-22.9 N (the Qasr Ibrim and Abu Simbel reach) to the Ayyubids. That is in line with the 1173-1175 Qasr Ibrim garrison, but the 943 found still draws those Makurian cells as Banu Kanz.
